title: [NatWest demo] Chaos injection audit
description:
Emits ONE ITSI notable for every nwpay:chaos event (action=inject or action=clear) so each incident.sh subcommand AND every click on the SPA Chaos Dashboard surfaces a row in Episode Review (ITSI Event Analytics). This is the SOC-on-stage signal that the audience watches scroll past as the presenter triggers scenarios: detection-and-attribution evidence that every production-touching action was logged AND classified by the SIEM, regardless of who triggered it (presenter via SPA, ops via CLI, or chaos-controller itself during recover()).

Severity mapping:
  * inject -> high (5)   (a new chaos is in progress; opens an Episode)
  * clear  -> info (1)   (chaos resolved; attaches to the open Episode as the 'all clear' marker)

Service mapping (drives Episode grouping and which L2 tile turns red):
  * api-gateway + details.tier=bronze/silver/gold -> Customer Tier Experience
  * fraud-detection-service + scenario=gold-fast-path-off -> Customer Tier Experience
  * fraud-detection-service, sanctions-aml-service -> Business Services
  * payment-*-service                              -> Payment Services
  * swift-network and other *-network              -> Payment Networks
  * ledger-service, postgres, redis, kafka         -> Ledger & Settlement Services
  * traffic-generator (madrid-network-degradation) -> Payments by Location
  * multi (recover-all)                            -> NatWest Card Payments (L1)
  * fallback                                       -> NatWest Card Payments

Dedupe: cohort_key is bound to the HEC-issued event_id, which is unique per call from both incident.sh AND chaos-controller/app/audit.py, so a re-run of this search inside the 3-minute lookback can never double-emit. The complementary chaos_off_change_window.json correlation search continues to emit a SECOND notable when an inject happens outside Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00 UTC; the two notables roll up into the same Episode (correlation_field=service in payments_episode_policy.json) so Episode Review shows one ticket with two attached events: 'chaos was injected' + 'chaos was injected OFF-WINDOW'. That dual signal is intentional - the compliance story benefits from seeing both detections.

": " . coalesce(scenario, "unknown-scenario") . " on " . coalesce(target_service, "unknown") . if(isnotnull(chaos_tier) AND chaos_tier!="", " (tier=" . chaos_tier .
